name: iq2i/vigie-bundle
description: A structured, queryable activity log for Symfony, written as ECS NDJSON with zero database — and, opt-in, a detection/response loop with a SIEM

suggest.phpunit/phpunit: To use the assertions shipped in IQ2i\VigieBundle\Test (see doc/testing.md)
suggest.symfony/console: To use the vigie:* console commands
suggest.symfony/http-client: To poll a SIEM's decisions with the built-in CrowdSec provider (see doc/threat.md)
suggest.symfony/lock: To prevent overlapping vigie:threat:sync runs on the same host (see doc/threat.md)
suggest.symfony/messenger: To correlate an activity recorded inside a Messenger handler with the request that dispatched it (see doc/recording.md)
suggest.symfony/monolog-bundle: To configure a custom Monolog handler for iq2i_vigie.output.handlers (see doc/storage.md)
suggest.symfony/routing: To redirect to a route from iq2i_vigie.threat.enforce.remediations, or to expose the threat ingest endpoint by importing @IQ2iVigieBundle/config/routes.php (see doc/threat.md)
suggest.symfony/security-csrf: To record CSRF token failures outside the login form (see doc/recording.md)
suggest.symfony/security-http: To track login, logout and switch user events
suggest.symfony/uid: To generate RFC 4122 request ids for correlation instead of falling back to random bytes
suggest.symfony/web-profiler-bundle: To show the Vigie panel in the debug toolbar
